explanation: Compared against OEIS A230241: a(n) is the number of ways to write n = p + q with q ≥ 1 and p, 3p - 10, (p-1)q - 1 all prime. Zhi-Wei Sun conjectured a(n) > 0 for all n > 5. The definition sums over 1 ≤ p < n, so q = n - p ≥ 1. Truncated subtraction for p ≤ 3 gives 3p - 10 = 0, which is not prime, matching the integer meaning; (p-1)q - 1 does not truncate for primes p. The tests match the data. The statement asserts a n > 0 for n > 5. Faithful.
